entities.title: Gen Z protests in Kathmandu and other cities, 8 September 2025

properties.summary: Day-long protests against the social media ban and corruption. A rally began at Maitighar Mandala at about 9 am and moved to New Baneshwar, where it reached the Federal Parliament. Police and armed police used tear gas, water cannon, rubber bullets and live fire; a curfew was imposed from 12:30 pm. Nineteen deaths were reported nationwide by night (17 in Kathmandu, 2 in Itahari) and between 340 and 400+ injured, with protests also in Pokhara, Itahari, Butwal, Bhairahawa, Damak, Biratnagar and Chitwan. The Home Minister resigned that evening and the cabinet lifted the social media ban late that night.

evidence.note: Parent event for the 8 September sub-events.

19 is the figure most outlets reached by night of 8 September (17 Kathmandu + 2 Itahari per Kathmandu Post and ANI). All India Radio gives 16 in Kathmandu Valley + 2 Itahari while stating 19; later counts for 8-9 September combined are higher and are covered by other agents.

entities.title: Rally gathers at Maitighar Mandala

properties.summary: Demonstrators, many in school or college uniform and calling themselves Gen Z, gathered at Maitighar in central Kathmandu from about 9 am. The Kathmandu Post photo story says the rally was organised by the Hami Nepal group with prior approval; leaders urged no vandalism, arson or violence.

evidence.note: Organiser attribution (Hami Nepal) appears in the Kathmandu Post photo story only.

entities.title: Rally marches from Maitighar to New Baneshwar

properties.summary: By mid-morning the rally moved toward New Baneshwar with songs and banners. Protesters tore down posters of the then prime minister near Bijuli Bazaar. By noon thousands occupied the traffic island at Baneshwar and gathered outside the Parliament building.

evidence.note: Times are given as 'mid-morning' and 'by noon'; one published account (Kathmandu Post, repeated by ANN).

entities.title: First police barricades breached; water cannon and tear gas used

properties.summary: Per Harvard's Atrocity Prevention Lab timeline, demonstrators breached the first police barricades by 11:38 am, security forces deployed water cannon, and tear gas followed at 11:55 am. Human Rights Watch says police used tear gas, water cannon and batons as marchers pressed against barricades.

evidence.note: Exact minutes (11:38, 11:55) come from the Harvard timeline only; the use of tear gas and water cannon before the shooting is confirmed by HRW and others.

entities.title: Protesters climb Parliament gate and walls

properties.summary: Around twenty people had climbed the main gate of the Federal Parliament by 12:08 pm, per Harvard; the Kathmandu Post says some youths climbed the walls to plant the national flag; Himalayan Times says protesters broke into restricted zones and entered the premises. HRW says police fired after people climbed on the wall outside Parliament.

evidence.note: Reports differ on how far protesters got (gate, wall, or inside the premises).

entities.title: Police fire on protesters at Parliament and New Baneshwar

properties.summary: Police and armed police used tear gas, water cannon, rubber bullets and live ammunition. Firing came from inside the Parliament compound, including by the Special Task Force with INSAS and SLR rifles (Kathmandu Post). HRW documents lethal force between about 12:30 and 4 pm. The start time of the shooting is reported as 12:37 pm (Harvard), after a 12:40 pm radio order (BBC, via Ratopati), or just before 1 pm (Kathmandu Post). Seventeen died in Kathmandu hospitals by night.

evidence.note: Start time and who gave the order are contested: see claims first-shots-at-12-37, gunfire-began-just-before-1pm, peter-one-radio-order-12-40.
17 deaths in Kathmandu are given by Kathmandu Post, Himal Press and HRW. Earlier counts were lower (1, 2, 6, 8, 14) as the day went on. All India Radio's 16 in the Valley differs.

entities.title: Journalist shot while reporting near Parliament

properties.summary: Harvard's timeline records that a Naya Patrika journalist was shot while reporting at 1:20 pm. INSEC's report says police gunfire affected protesters and journalists.

evidence.note: Journalist is not named in the cited text.

entities.title: Police fire tear gas inside Civil Service Hospital compound

properties.summary: Around 3 pm police entered the Civil Service Hospital premises in New Baneshwar and fired tear gas, per Harvard. HRW's 9 September statement also says tear gas was used at Civil Hospital, where some of the injured were taken.

evidence.note: The 3 pm time is from Harvard only; HRW gives no time.

entities.title: Kathmandu hospitals receive dead and injured protesters

properties.summary: Civil Service Hospital, the National Trauma Centre, Everest Hospital, Kathmandu Medical College and Tribhuvan University Teaching Hospital received the dead and injured. HRW reports Civil Service Hospital treated 221 injured patients and the Trauma Centre received 8 dead or later dead. The per-hospital death split differs between outlets.

evidence.note: See claims hospital-split-8-3-3-2-1 and hospital-split-himalpress-6-5-3-2-1.

entities.title: Police fire on protesters in Itahari

properties.summary: Protesters arrested youths involved in arson at the sub-metropolitan city office; demonstrators then marched to the Area Police Office and threw stones, and police opened fire, killing two men estimated at 25 and 30. The injured were taken to BP Koirala Institute of Health Sciences in Dharan. A curfew followed in Itahari.

evidence.note: No hour is given in the cited articles. Himal Press says police acted after demonstrators marched to the Area Police Office; Republica says after youths were arrested for arson.

entities.title: Gen Z protest clash in Pokhara

properties.summary: Protesters gathered in the area of the Chief Minister and Council of Ministers office and vandalised a government vehicle, after which police used tear gas and batons. INSEC reports 30 injured, five by police gunfire. The Kaski district administration imposed an indefinite prohibitory order from 2 pm.

evidence.note: Injury figures from INSEC only.

entities.title: Gen Z protest in Damak

properties.summary: ANI reports that in Damak (Jhapa) protesters attempted to break municipal gates and set fire to several motorcycles, and that police responded with water cannon, tear gas and rubber bullets.

evidence.note: Both articles are the same ANI wire.

entities.title: Gen Z protests in Butwal and Bhairahawa

properties.summary: Protests escalated in the Butwal-Bhairahawa area and the Rupandehi district administration imposed a curfew from 4 pm to 10 pm.

evidence.note: Curfew time from Himalayan Times only; the existence of protests in Butwal is reported by Kathmandu Post and Himalayan Times.

entities.title: Gen Z protests in Biratnagar, Chitwan and other cities

properties.summary: Kathmandu Post lists protests in Pokhara, Biratnagar, Janakpur, Hetauda and Nepalgunj; Himalayan Times lists Biratnagar, Butwal, Chitwan and Pokhara and reports curfews in Biratnagar (11 am to 10 pm), Birgunj (11 am to 6 pm) and Kavrepalanchok (from 12:15 pm).

evidence.note: Cities listed differ between outlets.

entities.title: Home Minister Ramesh Lekhak resigns

properties.summary: Lekhak submitted his resignation to Prime Minister Oli during the cabinet meeting at Baluwatar on Monday evening, citing moral grounds, after pressure from Nepali Congress leaders.

evidence.note: Evening of 8 September; Sharesansar published 8:19 PM and the Kathmandu Post updated 20:40.

entities.title: Cabinet meeting at the prime minister's residence, Baluwatar

properties.summary: An emergency cabinet meeting took place on Monday evening at Baluwatar. Lekhak resigned during it, a probe committee was decided, and a later late-night meeting decided to lift the social media ban.

evidence.note: Reports mention an evening meeting (Kathmandu Post, All India Radio) and an emergency or late-night meeting (AFP, blue News); they may be the same sitting continuing into the night.

entities.title: Government announces the social media ban is lifted

properties.summary: After an emergency cabinet meeting, Communication Minister Prithvi Subba Gurung was quoted as saying the government had withdrawn the ban. Al Jazeera says this was late on Monday night; AFP datelines it as Tuesday, a day after the deaths, and found major apps working in Kathmandu.

evidence.note: Date conflict: late Monday night (Al Jazeera) vs Tuesday (AFP). Likely the same overnight decision; see claims ban-lifted-late-monday-night and ban-lifted-on-tuesday.

entities.title: Congress and opposition leaders hold Oli responsible

properties.summary: On the night of 8 September, Nepali Congress general secretary Gagan Thapa said the prime minister must take responsibility and called for the party to leave the government; senior Congress leaders including Shekhar Koirala made similar calls and the CPN (Maoist Centre) demanded Oli's resignation.

evidence.note: Thapa's Facebook post is dated the morning of 9 September in Setopati; the Kathmandu Post (via ANN) places the statement on the night of the 8th.

entities.title: Curfew order around New Baneshwar, 12:30 pm to 10 pm

properties.description: Kathmandu District Administration Office imposed a curfew from 12:30 pm to 10 pm covering Baneshwor Chowk to Bijuli Bazar bridge (west), Tinkune Chowk (east), Ratna Rajya School (north) and Shankhamul bridge (south). HRW notes the government ordered the curfew at around 12:30 pm; Kathmandu Post says few in the crowd heard the order.

evidence.note: The 12:30 pm start is stated by six outlets. The Kathmandu Post's 19-dead article says 'a curfew from 3:30 pm' (see claim curfew-from-3-30-pm). Cause: protesters entering the Parliament area (Himalayan Times).

entities.title: Curfew extended to Singha Durbar, Parliament, presidential and vice-presidential offices

properties.description: Curfew extended to the administrative core of Kathmandu, including Singha Durbar, the Parliament building, the offices of the President and Vice President and the Narayanhiti Museum area (Himal Press); ANI adds the prime minister's residence. INSEC lists Baneshwor, Singha Durbar, Baluwatar and Sheetal Niwas.

evidence.note: Time of the extension is not given by any of the three. Issuer is the district administration per ANI/Himal Press ('local administration').

entities.title: Nepali Army deployed in New Baneshwor

properties.description: Himalayan Times, at 1:25 pm, reports the Nepali Army was deployed in New Baneshwor as the situation intensified.

evidence.note: The 13:25 time is the article's publication time, not necessarily the deployment time.

entities.title: Indefinite prohibitory order in Pokhara from 2 pm

properties.description: Kaski District Administration imposed an indefinite prohibitory order in the Pokhara area bounded by Shahid Chowk, Milan Chowk, Fistel Gate (Baidam), the Land Revenue Office and Rastrabank Chowk, from 2 pm until further notice. Kantipur separately reports an indefinite curfew order.

evidence.note: The 2 pm time appears in Onlinekhabar only; Kantipur gives no time.

entities.title: Curfew in Butwal-Bhairahawa, 4 pm to 10 pm

properties.description: Rupandehi District Administration Office imposed a curfew order in the Butwal-Bhairahawa area from 4 pm to 10 pm, under Section 6(A) of the Local Administration Act, 2028.

entities.title: Curfews in Biratnagar, Birgunj and Kavrepalanchok

properties.description: Himalayan Times reports curfews in Koshi Province's Biratnagar (11 am to 10 pm), Birgunj (11 am to 6 pm, extended) and Kavrepalanchok (from 12:15 pm), and in Kathmandu and Lalitpur areas.

evidence.note: Issuing office not named in the article; no issued_by link is made.

entities.title: Home Minister Ramesh Lekhak resigns

properties.description: Lekhak tendered his resignation to Prime Minister Oli during the Cabinet meeting at Baluwatar on Monday evening, on moral grounds, after Nepali Congress leaders called for it.

entities.title: Cabinet withdraws the social media ban

properties.description: After an emergency cabinet meeting the government withdrew the ban and the ministry ordered agencies to resume social media. Communication Minister Prithvi Subba Gurung was quoted by local media. AFP found all major apps working in Kathmandu on Tuesday.

evidence.note: Date is late Monday night (Al Jazeera) or Tuesday (AFP); blue News calls the announcing minister the Home Minister, which conflicts with AFP and with Lekhak having resigned as Home Minister.

entities.title: Cabinet forms committee to investigate the violence

properties.description: The Monday-evening cabinet meeting at Baluwatar decided to form an inquiry committee; All India Radio says terms of reference were to be submitted within 15 days. The Kathmandu Post (via ANN) says the government formed a probe committee.

evidence.note: Committee head and membership are not given in these sources.

entities.title: Hospitals instructed to treat injured protesters free

properties.description: All India Radio reports the Ministry of Health earlier instructed hospitals to provide free treatment to all injured protesters.

entities.title: NHRC urges restraint, relief and free treatment

properties.description: The National Human Rights Commission urged restraint and called on authorities to provide relief and compensation to victims' families and free treatment for the injured, according to ANI.

evidence.note: Direct NHRC text was not retrieved.

entities.title: Oli tells cabinet the protest was infiltrated

properties.description: According to the Kathmandu Post (via ANN), during the Monday cabinet meeting Oli said the peaceful demonstration was infiltrated by disruptive elements while expressing sensitivity toward youth demands.

evidence.note: Paraphrase from the article; no direct quote from Oli was retrieved.

entities.title: Peter one radio order 12 40

properties.statement: A police radio message from 'Peter One' at 12:40 pm, attributed to an order from Inspector General Chandra Kuber Khapung, told units to use force; police then fired from the Parliament premises.
properties.verification_note: Reported by Ratopati from a BBC investigation of radio logs and over 4,000 videos. The BBC article itself could not be fetched. Khapung and the District Security Committee chief deny giving such an order (see claim khapung-and-rijal-deny-issuing-fire-order). The home minister says he did not order firing (claim lekhak-did-not-order-police-to-fire). Harvard places the first shots at 12:37 pm, three minutes before the reported order.

evidence.note: Reported by Ratopati from a BBC investigation of radio logs and over 4,000 videos. The BBC article itself could not be fetched. Khapung and the District Security Committee chief deny giving such an order (see claim khapung-and-rijal-deny-issuing-fire-order). The home minister says he did not order firing (claim lekhak-did-not-order-police-to-fire). Harvard places the first shots at 12:37 pm, three minutes before the reported order.

entities.title: Khapung and rijal deny issuing fire order

properties.statement: Inspector General Chandra Kuber Khapung and the District Security Committee chief Chhabilal Rijal say they did not issue an order to fire.
properties.verification_note: Denial as reported by Ratopati citing the BBC. Registry id person:chhabi-rijal is used for Chhabilal Rijal on the basis of the name only; the source does not give his office beyond 'District Security Committee chief'.

evidence.note: Denial as reported by Ratopati citing the BBC. Registry id person:chhabi-rijal is used for Chhabilal Rijal on the basis of the name only; the source does not give his office beyond 'District Security Committee chief'.

entities.title: Lekhak did not order police to fire

properties.statement: Home Minister Ramesh Lekhak said he did not order police to open fire and had told them to use water cannon and batons only.
properties.verification_note: Statement quoted by Himal Press as he announced his resignation. No independent record of his instructions was found.

evidence.note: Statement quoted by Himal Press as he announced his resignation. No independent record of his instructions was found.

entities.title: Police compelled to fire after breach

properties.statement: Security officials said police were compelled to open fire after protesters breached a restricted area and tried to enter Parliament.
properties.verification_note: Himal Press attributes this to security officials. HRW says police fired directly at students and that lethal force was used between about 12:30 and 4 pm, and Amnesty says live fire was unlawful.

evidence.note: Himal Press attributes this to security officials. HRW says police fired directly at students and that lethal force was used between about 12:30 and 4 pm, and Amnesty says live fire was unlawful.

entities.title: Oli said protest was infiltrated

properties.statement: Prime Minister Oli told the cabinet the peaceful demonstration had been infiltrated by disruptive elements.
properties.verification_note: Paraphrase in the Kathmandu Post report via ANN; no direct Oli quote retrieved.

evidence.note: Paraphrase in the Kathmandu Post report via ANN; no direct Oli quote retrieved.

entities.title: First shots at 12 37

properties.statement: Police opened fire for the first time at 12:37 pm, at protesters who had climbed onto a small building near the Parliament gate.
properties.verification_note: Harvard timeline. The Kathmandu Post puts the start of gunfire just before 1 pm; the BBC (via Ratopati) puts the radio order at 12:40 pm; HRW gives a window from about 12:30 pm.

evidence.note: Harvard timeline. The Kathmandu Post puts the start of gunfire just before 1 pm; the BBC (via Ratopati) puts the radio order at 12:40 pm; HRW gives a window from about 12:30 pm.

entities.title: Gunfire began just before 1pm

properties.statement: Gunfire began just before 1 pm, from inside Parliament.
properties.verification_note: Kathmandu Post narrative. Harvard says 12:37 pm; BBC (via Ratopati) says the order was at 12:40 pm.

evidence.note: Kathmandu Post narrative. Harvard says 12:37 pm; BBC (via Ratopati) says the order was at 12:40 pm.

entities.title: Lethal force between 12 30 and 4pm

properties.statement: Police used lethal force between around 12:30 and 4 pm.
properties.verification_note: HRW's reconstruction from video and interviews; consistent with, and wider than, the Harvard and Kathmandu Post start times.

evidence.note: HRW's reconstruction from video and interviews; consistent with, and wider than, the Harvard and Kathmandu Post start times.

entities.title: Curfew from 12 30 pm

properties.statement: The Kathmandu district administration's curfew around New Baneshwar took effect at 12:30 pm and ran to 10 pm.
properties.verification_note: Stated by Kathmandu Post, HRW, ANI/Tribune, Himalayan Times, Harvard and Onlinekhabar.

evidence.note: Stated by Kathmandu Post, HRW, ANI/Tribune, Himalayan Times, Harvard and Onlinekhabar.

entities.title: Curfew from 3 30 pm

properties.statement: A curfew was in force from 3:30 pm.
properties.verification_note: Kathmandu Post's 19-dead article gives 3:30 pm in a general sentence about authorities. Six outlets give 12:30 pm for Kathmandu. A later or wider curfew order may exist; none was found for Kathmandu.

evidence.note: Kathmandu Post's 19-dead article gives 3:30 pm in a general sentence about authorities. Six outlets give 12:30 pm for Kathmandu. A later or wider curfew order may exist; none was found for Kathmandu.

entities.title: Shooting continued after curfew order

properties.statement: Firing and bloodshed continued on Baneshwar's streets after the curfew order was issued.
properties.verification_note: Kantipur: blood still flowing after the order. HRW places lethal force until about 4 pm and Kathmandu Post says few in the crowd heard the order.

evidence.note: Kantipur: blood still flowing after the order. HRW places lethal force until about 4 pm and Kathmandu Post says few in the crowd heard the order.

entities.title: Toll one dead early afternoon

properties.statement: One protester had died at Civil Hospital in New Baneshwor.
properties.verification_note: ANI report updated 02:40 pm IST (about 3:25 pm Nepal time). Early figure; superseded the same day.

evidence.note: ANI report updated 02:40 pm IST (about 3:25 pm Nepal time). Early figure; superseded the same day.

entities.title: Toll seventeen dead in kathmandu
